Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Kuldeep Mathur
 Order

The instant criminal miscellaneous petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner for quashing the FIR No.51/2019 registered at Women Police Station Pali for the offences under Sections 498A, 406 and 323 IPC.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the marriage of his son- Bhavishya was solemised with respondent No.2 on 06.02.2018 as per Hindu rites and rituals.

Soon after the marriage,
respondent No.2 started quarreling with her husband and other family members.
Learned counsel submitted that on their relations turning strained, a false FIR has been lodged by respondent No.2 against the petitioner and other family members under Section 498A, 406, 323 of IPC.
Learned counsel submitted [2023:RJ-JD:30569] (2 of 4) [CRLMP-4516/2019] that in the FIR, general omnibus allegations have been levelled against present petitioner and other family members.

It was urged that the petitioner and his wife disinherited their son Bhavishya and respondent No.2, by publishing general information in Dainik Bhaskar newspaper on 22.11.2018, despite this, only with a Rishi Kumar Singh vs State (2023:Rj-Jd:30569) on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115351983/
1 view to harass the petitioner, a captioned FIR has been lodged on 10.07.2019.
Learned counsel prayed that the impugned FIR and proceeding initiated in pursuance thereof, may be quashed and set aside.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the criminal miscellaneous petition and submitted that it is incorrect to state that omnibus allegations have been levelled against the petitioner by complainant-respondent No.2, only with a view to falsely implicate the petitioner in a criminal case.

Learned counsel jointly submitted that from the perusal of the FIR, it would reveal that complainant- respondent No.2 was harassed and humiliated at the hands of the petitioner and other family members who used to torture her mentally and physically.

Learned counsel jointly submitted that during the course of investigation,
the police has found the allegations to be correct and charge sheet against the husband Bhavishya has already been submitted before competent criminal court.
Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner disinherited his son in a pre-planned manner only with a view to save himself from legal action.
Learned counsel prayed that the present criminal miscellaneous petition may be dismissed by this Court.
[2023:RJ-JD:30569] (3 of 4) [CRLMP-4516/2019] Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
Perused the material available on record.

Hon'ble the Supreme Court of India in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal reported in AIR 1992 SC 604, held that the power of quashing a criminal proceeding in exercise of inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC should be invoked sparingly.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal reported in AIR 1992 SC 604
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Para 103 of the judgment is reproduced below for ready reference:-
"103.

We also give a note of caution to the effect that the power of quashing a criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases; that the court will not be justified in embarking upon an enquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and that the extraordinary or inherent powers do not confer an arbitrary jurisdiction on the court to act according to its whim or caprice."

On a close scrutiny of the FIR and factual report submitted by the Investigating Officer through Public Prosecutor, this Court finds that a cognizable offence has been made out against the petitioner in the investigation carried out by the investigating agency.
This Court also finds that specific allegation against the petitioner of torturing the complainant-respondent No.2 mentally and physically have been levelled.
This Court has no reason to believe that the FIR has been lodged to wreak vengeance against present petitioner.

It is to be noticed that this Court while exercising inherent powers under Section 482 CrPC cannot [2023:RJ-JD:30569] (4 of 4) [CRLMP-4516/2019]
examine the truthfulness and genuineness of the allegations levelled against the petitioner in great detail.

In wake of aforesaid, no case warranting interference in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 CrPC is made out and the instant criminal miscellaneous petition is dismissed being devoid of Rishi Kumar Singh vs State (2023:Rj-Jd:30569) on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115351983/
2 merit.
Stay application also stand disposed of.
